extracted.intended_audience: public housing agencies (PHAs), owners/managers of HUD-assisted project-based rental properties (PBRA), HUD program administrators, and housing legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and implementation guidance for a HUD final rule that mandates a 30-day written notification prior to filing a formal judicial eviction for nonpayment of rent in covered HUD-assisted housing programs, including required notice contents, timing, accessibility, and related lease amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-day written notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs and owners of properties receiving project-based rental assistance must provide written notification to tenants facing eviction for nonpayment of rent 30 days prior to filing a formal judicial eviction procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a minimum requirement; PHAs/owners may provide a longer notice if they choose. The rule covers specified HUD programs (see program coverage criterion). HUD will issue sample language PHAs/owners may use, but PHAs/owners may draft their own notices so long as they include the required contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programs covered by the rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule applies to PHAs and owners in multiple HUD programs including Section 8 Project-Based Rental Assistance, Section 202/162 Project Assistance Contract (PAC), Section 202 Project Rental Assistance Contract (PRAC), Section 811 PRAC, Section 811 Project Rental Assistance Program (811 PRA), Senior Preservation Rental Assistance Contract Projects (SPRAC), and related parts identified at 24 CFR parts 247, 880, 884, 886, 891, and 966.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain regulatory cites (e.g., 24 CFR 247.4, 880.606/880.607, 884.215/884.216, 886.127/886.327, 891.425, 966.4) were revised or added to implement the requirement; see rule text for program-specific compliance timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of notice relative to rent due date
rubrics_metrics.description: A PHA or owner must not provide tenants with a termination notice before the day after the rent is due according to the lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies when the 30‑day clock can begin; the notice must be provided after the rent due date and before filing a formal judicial eviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: No eviction filing if tenant cures within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: A PHA or owner must not proceed with filing an eviction if the tenant pays the alleged amount of rent owed within the 30-day notification period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of the alleged rent amount within the 30-day period bars filing a formal judicial eviction for nonpayment of rent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Itemized monthly rent owed in notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The 30-day notice must include an itemized amount, separated by month, of alleged rent owed by the tenant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itemizing rent by month is intended to reduce confusion about what is owed and when. The rule revises specific CFR sections to require monthly separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Itemized monthly arrearages (separate from rent)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 30-day notice must include any other arrearages allowed by HUD and included in the lease, separated by month, and those arrearages must be itemized separately from the alleged rent amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrearages might include late fees or other fees; listing them separately helps tenants understand obligations. HUD notes some HUD programs prohibit evictions for certain non-rent fees (see 'limitations on evictions for certain arrearages').

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment deadline to avoid eviction
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must state the date by which the tenant must pay the amount of rent owed before a formal judicial eviction can be filed for nonpayment of rent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must clearly communicate the cutoff date for curing nonpayment to prevent filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions to cure nonpayment lease violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must include instructions on how tenants can cure lease violations for nonpayment of rent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD previously proposed and the final rule requires instructions so tenants understand actions that will cure the violation (e.g., payment, repayment agreement, recertification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information on recertification and hardship exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must include information on how tenants can recertify their income and how tenants can request a minimum rent hardship exemption, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs/owners must process interim reexamination/recertification requests within a reasonable time; the notice should direct tenants to these options as potential remedies to avoid eviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to offer repayment agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD strongly recommends the best practice of entering into a rental repayment agreement as an alternative to requiring a lump-sum payment for past due amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs/owners are encouraged (and PHAs are required to include information about switching from flat rent to income-based rent) to offer repayment agreements to prevent evictions; HUD suggests repayment agreements reduce the need for eviction filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include switching information from flat to income-based rent
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs must include information in the 30-day notification about how to switch from flat rent to income-based rent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement helps tenants understand options that may reduce their rent obligations and avoid eviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and LEP (meaningful access) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The 30-day notice must be provided in accessible formats to ensure effective communication for individuals with disabilities and in a form to allow meaningful access for individuals with limited English proficiency (LEP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs and owners must comply with Title VI (national origin/LEP) guidance and Section 504 accessibility requirements; HUD references its 2007 Title VI/LEP guidance and requires meaningful access and effective communication steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodations notice and point of contact
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD suggests that the 30-day notice advise individuals of their right to request reasonable accommodations, include information on how individuals with disabilities can request a reasonable accommodation, and include a point of contact for reasonable accommodation requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs/owners are required to provide reasonable accommodations (and modifications where required) unless it would cause undue financial/administrative burden or fundamental alteration; notices should inform tenants how to seek accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs and owners must comply with nondiscrimination requirements contained in Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, along with HUD's implementing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title VI's requirements regarding meaningful access for LEP persons are highlighted; fair housing and ADA/Section 504 obligations (including reasonable modifications/accommodations) also apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does not preempt state/local laws offering greater protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule sets a Federal minimum and does not preempt any State or local law that provides greater or equal protection for tenants; the 30-day notice may run consecutive to any additional State or local notice requirements if required by State or local law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs/owners must still comply with state/local tenant laws that are more protective or require additional notices; HUD intends the rule to standardize the minimum across HUD programs without displacing higher protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease amendment and tenant notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs and owners must amend all current and future leases to incorporate the 30-day notice requirement for nonpayment of rent and provide tenants with notification of changes to the lease under existing regulatory requirements (e.g., 24 CFR 880.607(d) and 966.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When modifying leases, owners must serve appropriate notice to tenants at least 30 days prior to the last date the tenant may terminate tenancy; PHAs must provide opportunity for tenant comments per existing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on applicability to non-rent lease violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Protections in this rule do not apply to other types of evictions that result from non-rent lease violations, such as eviction for nonpayment of arrearages if allowed under the applicable HUD program and specified in the lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD clarifies evictions for certain non-rent fees or other lease violations may not be covered; guidance and program handbooks (e.g., HUD Handbook 4350.3) explain specific prohibitions (e.g., owners must not evict for failure to pay late charges in some programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Itemization includes late fees and non-rent fees where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Any arrearages, which might include late fees or other fees, must be itemized separately from the alleged rent amount in the 30-day notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD references existing policy on non-rent fees for subsidized multifamily and public housing programs; itemization is intended to reduce tenant confusion about amounts owed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHAs/owners must process interim reexamination requests reasonably
rubrics_metrics.description: When a tenant requests an interim reexamination (e.g., due to reduced income), the PHA or owner must process this request within a reasonable time, and the 30-day notice should inform tenants of this option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim reexamination and rent recalculation can change rent amounts and help prevent eviction; tenants should be informed about how to request and pursue these remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance dates and phased implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with the rule is required no later than January 13, 2025, except that PHA compliance with 24 CFR 966.4(q) is required no later than June 15, 2026; PBRA owner compliance with certain requirements is required no later than 14 months from HUD's publication of final model leases incorporating these requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs and owners should track program-specific compliance timelines and integrate changes into leases and procedures accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: HUD-provided sample language and PHAs/owners' discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD will issue sample language PHAs and owners may use for the 30-day notice; however, PHAs and owners may draft their own notices as long as they include the required contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of HUD sample language is optional; the critical requirement is inclusion of all mandated elements and compliance with timing, accessibility, and nondiscrimination obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of rule provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD intends the provisions of this rule to operate independently; if any portion is declared invalid as to a particular program, HUD intends other unaffected provisions to remain valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a legal drafting principle clarifying that portions of the regulation can remain in force even if other parts are invalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content suggestions and optional elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters and HUD identified additional suggested elements and clarifications to include in notice content: balance information, Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) information, interim recertification and hardship exemption procedures, legal and rental assistance resources, repayment agreement options, and information on accessibility and reasonable accommodations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While some of these items are required (e.g., recertification, hardship exemption information), others are recommended best practices to improve tenant understanding and reduce preventable eviction filings.
